Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation / SLO follow-up

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can validate Dedicated capacity against AtlasHealth's SLOs.

Summary of goals we heard on the call:
- P99 latency target: <= 250ms for streaming chat responses (typical response lengths ~200–12 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: ~50 RPS (end-user requests per second), with bursts to 100 RPS expected during peak minutes.
- Concurrency: roughly 20–30 active concurrent sessions for live chat; up to 100 total concurrent background inference calls (batching tolerant).
- Streaming: client expects chunked/streamed tokens (partial results within 50–100ms per chunk).

What we propose for a dedicated performance validation run:
1) Validation plan + data: you provide a representative sample set (CSV of prompts, distribution of token lengths, and a short list of models to test).
2) Run 1-hour sustained tests on two HW profiles: 4x H100 (80GB) nodes vs. 8x A100 (40GB) nodes to compare p50/p95/p99, tail latency, GPU utilization, and token throughput.
3) Streaming-specific tests: measure end-to-end chunk latency and time-to-first-byte for the streaming path; test with 50RPS sustained + 100RPS burst.
4) Deliverables: detailed results (latency percentiles, throughput curves), recommended reserved-throughput sizing, and a configuration for reserved capacity (autoscale/burst knobs).

Preliminary sizing notes (high level) — we'll validate these in the run:
- For the streaming SLOs you described, H100-backed nodes generally give better tail latency for large models and high-concurrency streaming.
- We typically size reserved throughput to cover sustained RPS + safety buffer (eg. reserved = 1.2x sustained). For 50 RPS sustained that implies reserved throughput ~60 RPS with bursts allowed to 100 RPS.

Next steps:
- Can you share a 1–2 hour sample of production traffic (anonymized prompts + typical token-length histogram) and confirm preferred test window next week (we have slots Tue–Thu 06/28–06/30 PST).
- We'll send a short PoC plan and test harness (attached) and schedule a 30-minute kickoff with Aditya (Solutions Eng) to align on observability and tracing hooks.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf, redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks — I'll coordinate availability once you confirm the sample data and preferred window.

—Marissa

Hi Alex — thanks for the questions. Short answers and a pragmatic validation config below. Happy to discuss in the kickoff.

1) p99 <= 200ms for streaming time-to-first-byte: that is tight for 200–12 token responses. A few levers to hit that: smaller chunk sizes (we typically stream 32–64 token chunks), aggressive prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and ensuring the client renders partial chunks immediately. If time-to-first-byte is the metric, we're more likely to hit ~120–180ms on H100 for shorter responses; for longer or complex generation the tail will stretch. We should validate with your real prompt set.

2) Reserved throughput model: reserved pools are designed for sustained RPS. For mixed workloads (interactive + background) we recommend one reserved pool sized for interactive sustained load (50 RPS) and a shared burst pool for background callers. That keeps your SLA for live chat while allowing cost-effective handling of background jobs.

3) HW guidance (practical):
- H100 (80GB) profile: better tail latency and higher single-request throughput for larger models / streaming. For your SLOs, a 4x H100 node pool as the initial reserved cluster is a good starting point.
- A100 (40GB) profile: lower cost but you'll need larger count and may see higher tail latency under streaming. Our rough starting configs for the validation run:
  - H100-run: 4 × H100 nodes, reserved throughput configured to 60 RPS (1.2x sustained), burst to 120 RPS.
  - A100-run: 8 × A100 nodes, reserved throughput 70 RPS, burst to 140 RPS (to account for lower per-GPU throughput).

Actionable validation plan (what Redwood will provide):
- Test harness that replays your anonymized traffic with realistic concurrency and chunking behavior.
- Per-request tracing for latency breakdown (network, decode, kernel exec, queueing).
- Post-run report with p50/p95/p99 and recommended reserved sizing + cost estimate.

If you can drop the traffic sample, I'll prepare the test harness and tentative slot for Tue 06/28 09:00 PST.
